newsitem.title: USA: Hughes wins major contract for new U.S. missile.
newsitem.headline: Hughes wins major contract for new U.S. missile.

text.p: The U.S. military on Friday awarded a $169.2 million contract to Hughes Missiles Systems Co. to develop a successor to the AIM-9M Sidewinder missile used by fighter jets against enemy aircraft.

Hughes, owned by General Motors Corp., won a competition with Raytheon Co. which could mean $5 billion in eventual sales of the new short-range AIM-9X and vault the United States ahead of "dog fighting" air-to-air missiles built by other nations.
The new heat-seeking missile would replace a missile carried by U.S. and allied warplanes in various versions for more than 30 years.

The Sidewinder, last updated after the 1991 Gulf War, is the Pentagon's only such short-range missile for Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps fighters and is now considered inferior to more modern foreign air-to-air missiles, including Russia's AA-11 "Archer".

The contract awarded to Hughes on Friday was for development of the new AIM-9X over five years and the Pentagon said it could reach a total of $252.5 million if additional development options are exercised during that period.
But actual production will mean far more money. The U.S. military alone is expected to buy a total of the 10,000 of the new missiles in the next century.
